summary:
LOST IN SPACE is an immersive, web-based 3D storytelling experience developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It brings attention to the often-overlooked stories of NASA's exploration equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars.

Our project transforms the histories of three remarkable missions into an interactive journey: the Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV), the twin Mars rovers Spirit and Opportunity, and the Ingenuity Mars Helicopter. Through immersive 3D environments, animations, synchronized narration, and accessible scientific information, visitors can explore the purpose, achievements, discoveries, and eventual fate of these machines.

By turning NASA's mission histories into engaging visual stories, LOST IN SPACE directly addresses the challenge of making the legacy of abandoned space equipment more accessible and meaningful. It is important because these machines were not simply left behind; they played essential roles in expanding our understanding of other worlds. Our goal is to inspire younger generations to explore science, engineering, and space while ensuring that the stories of these machines are not forgotten.
details:
Project Details – LOST IN SPACE

LOST IN SPACE is an immersive, web-based 3D storytelling experience that brings the overlooked stories of NASA's exploration equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars to life.

The project works through a guided scrolling journey divided into three chapters, featuring the Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV), NASA's twin Mars rovers Spirit and Opportunity, and the Ingenuity Mars Helicopter. Each chapter combines 3D visuals, animations, synchronized narration, and scientific information to tell the story of each machine, explaining its purpose, achievements, discoveries, and eventual fate.

Benefits and Intended Impact:

The project makes space exploration history more accessible and engaging, especially for younger audiences. It encourages curiosity about science, engineering, robotics, and planetary exploration while highlighting the contributions of machines that helped humanity understand other worlds.

Tools and Development:

The project was developed as an HTML-based website. Our team used Claude and ChatGPT as AI-assisted tools for brainstorming, developing and refining narratives, generating and reviewing code, debugging, and improving the overall experience. All AI-assisted outputs were reviewed and adapted by the team.

Creativity and Innovation:

Our main creative approach is transforming historical NASA mission information into an immersive visual storytelling journey. Instead of simply reading facts, visitors experience the stories through interactive 3D environments, animations, and narration.

Design Considerations:

Throughout development, we considered scientific accuracy, historical authenticity, ease of understanding, visual engagement, storytelling quality, website performance, readability, and accessibility across desktop and mobile devices.
